Sam (ml-eng): Hey, bringing up a HF model on Redwood Dedicated and hit a puzzling tokenization mismatch. Generation offsets are wrong and special token alignments break. Anyone seen unicode/normalization issues in conversion?
Priya (ml-infra): @Sam can you paste a minimal repro? is this with the fast tokenizer? :thinking_face: 
Sam (ml-eng): Using AutoTokenizer from transformers (fast) -> token ids differ from HF inference vs Redwood runtime. Example:
```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
t = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('org/new-chat-model', use_fast=True)
print(t.encode('fiancé'))
print(t.encode('fiance\u0301'))  # precomposed vs decomposed
```
Results are different length / id mapping. On Redwood side the conversion util saved tokenizer.json without the normalizer metadata, so it decanonicalized.
Jonas (runtime): Hmm. That smells like NFC vs NFD. Our Redwood tokenizer loader expects the tokenizer.json to include normalizer config. Some HF tokenizers rely on huggingface/normalizers which are only in tokenizer.json 'normalizer' field. If missing, our fallback is a byte-fallback path which explodes lengths.
Carla (evals): This caused a measurable eval regression in our chat-turn-level metrics — exact-match dropped 6% in a few test prompts that contain accents/ligatures/emoji. We thought quantization affected it at first, but the tokenization mismatch explains many errors.
Priya (ml-infra): Quick checks: 1) Is the original tokenizer using `normalize=True`? 2) Did the conversion script set `tokenizer.backend` (rust/python) correctly? 3) Any special tokens like `<|user|>` mapped differently?
Sam (ml-eng): Answers: 1) HF tokenizer had `normalizer` config (NFC). 2) Our redwood-hf-converter silently dropped `normalizer` when tokenizers were saved as legacy files. 3) Yes — role tokens are contiguous byte sequences, and when pre-tokenization splits differently the special token match fails.
Jonas (runtime): For a short-term patch, we can force-normalize inputs on the Redwood side before tokenizing: `text = unicodedata.normalize('NFC', text)`. That recovers alignment for most cases. But long-term we should preserve the tokenizer.normalizer config during conversion.
Sam (ml-eng): Test I ran: with pre-normalize I get identical ids to HF: `unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)` before `tokenize`. But it breaks emoji fallback behavior for some legacy tokenizers that use byte fallback, e.g., isolated ZWJ sequences.
Carla (evals): Note: byte-fallback tokenizers (BPE+byte-level fallback) will produce different token counts if unicode is decomposed vs composed, and that changes quantization perf metrics (shorter sequences -> different activation patterns). So we need to rerun a small evaluation suite after fix.
Priya (ml-infra): Action items proposal: 1) Update conversion util to copy `normalizer` and `pre_tokenizer` from HF tokenizer.json when present. 2) Add a Redwood conversion flag `--force-normalizer` to include explicit normalization steps. 3) Add unit tests with ligatures, accents, emojis, ZWJ sequences.
Jonas (runtime): I'll add a small runtime opt-in: `REDWOOD_TOKENIZER_NORMALIZE=NFC` env var that applies normalize() at the API gateway for Dedicated/private until conversion is fixed.
Ava (infra-bot): Deploy check: added env var option to tokenization service schema, feature flag `tokenizer-normalize-nfc` set to off by default.
Sam (ml-eng): Also found one more gotcha — special token serialization. HF sometimes stores special tokens in `special_tokens_map.json` and expects exact byte sequences. Our converter mapped them to unicode-escaped strings which broke string matching. Example: "<|assistant|>" became "\u003c|assistant|\u003e" in tokenizer.json and didn't match. 
Priya (ml-infra): Ugh. That's why the simple string equality failed. We should preserve raw strings, not escape HTML-like tokens.
Carla (evals): I'll make a small prompt set focused on normalization edge cases (accents, combining marks, multi-codepoint emoji, whitespace variants) so we can detect regressions in CI.
Sam (ml-eng): Repro script (very small) to add to repo: 
```bash
python - <<'PY'
import unicodedata
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
T='org/new-chat-model'
t=AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(T, use_fast=True)
for s in ['fiancé','fiance\u0301','👩\u200d👩\u200d👧','\u00A0',' '] :
    print(s.encode('utf-8'), 'normNFC', t.encode(unicodedata.normalize('NFC', s)), 'raw', t.encode(s))
PY
```
Results should help decide if conversion or runtime normalization is correct.
Jonas (runtime): Nicely scoped. I'll land the env var and a short-term docs note. Priya, can you update the converter? I can add the unit tests Carla mentioned.
Priya (ml-infra): Yep — will prioritize converter fix and preserve `normalizer` + `pre_tokenizer` + `special_tokens` raw strings. I'll also add an automated conversion validation step that loads the converted tokenizer and compares token ids for a small canonical set.
Carla (evals): After fixes, we should rerun the quantization sweep. If tokenization changes, quantized model evals are not comparable to previous runs. Marking this as root cause for regression tickets.
Sam (ml-eng): Thanks all. Putting a short note in the model bring-up checklist: 1) verify normalizer config roundtrip 2) preserve special token raw strings 3) run normalization-edge evals. Saves debugging time later :relieved:
